sentences.ko: 그래서, 그 사람 진짜 또 만날 거야?
sentences.text: So, are you actually going to see her again?

alts.text: Wait, you're really seeing her again?
Do you intend to see her again?

sentences.note: **actually** 는 '실제로'라는 뜻보다 '진짜로?' 하는 확인·놀람에 가깝습니다. 상대가 그럴 줄 몰랐을 때 질문 안에 넣어 씁니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 5 | Friends

sentences.ko: 진짜라니까, 저 여자가 나한테 완전 윙크했다니까.
sentences.text: I'm telling you, that girl totally winked at me.

alts.text: No joke, she totally winked at me.
I assure you, that woman winked at me.

sentences.note: **I'm telling you** 는 상대가 안 믿을 것 같을 때 앞에 붙이는 '진짜라니까'입니다. **totally** 는 '완전히'가 아니라 '진짜, 완전' 정도의 강조로 말할 때만 씁니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 3 | Friends

sentences.ko: 넌 그냥 해야 할 일을 한 것뿐이야.
sentences.text: You just did what you had to do.

alts.text: Look, you had no choice.
There was nothing else you could have done.

sentences.note: **did what you had to do** 는 어쩔 수 없는 선택을 하고 마음이 무거운 사람을 다독일 때 씁니다. '잘했어'가 아니라 '어쩔 수 없었잖아'에 가깝습니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 5 | Friends

sentences.text: So, now everybody's going to kiss but me.

alts.text: Great, everyone gets a kiss except me.
It seems that everyone except me will be kissing.

sentences.note: 여기서 **but me** 의 but 은 '그러나'가 아니라 '~만 빼고'입니다. everybody, everyone, nobody, all 뒤에 붙여 '나만 빼고'를 짧게 말할 때 씁니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 1 | Friends

sentences.ko: 그냥 그 사람 만나서 좋은 점이랑 안 좋은 점을 한번 저울질해 보는 게 어때?
sentences.text: Why don't you just weigh out the good stuff about the relationship against the bad stuff?

alts.text: Just line up the good and the bad and see which side wins.
Perhaps you should weigh the advantages of the relationship against the disadvantages.

sentences.note: **weigh out** 은 두 가지를 저울에 올려 견줘 본다는 말이라 뒤에 against 가 따라옵니다. **Why don't you just** 는 조언을 가볍게 툭 던질 때 쓰는 말머리입니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones That Make You Laugh: Part 3 | Friends

sentences.text: We didn't know how you were going to react.

alts.text: Wasn't sure how you'd take it.
It was unclear to us how you would respond.

sentences.note: **how you were going to react** 는 상대가 어떻게 나올지 몰라 조심스러웠다고 할 때 씁니다. 나쁜 소식을 늦게 전한 이유를 댈 때 자주 나오고, 더 편하게는 **how you'd take it** 이라고 합니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 5 | Friends

sentences.ko: 아빠에 대해서 네가 모르던 게 하나 있어.
sentences.text: There's something you didn't know about your dad.

alts.text: Turns out you didn't know everything about your dad.
You were not aware of something about your father.

sentences.note: **There's something you didn't know** 는 상대가 몰랐던 사실을 꺼내기 전에 두는 서두입니다. 바로 본론을 말하면 놀라니까 한 박자 쉬어 가는 자리예요.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 10 | Friends

sentences.ko: 너 걔 화나게 할 만한 짓 한 거 없어?
sentences.text: Uh, did you do anything to make her mad?

alts.text: Any chance you upset her?
Is there anything you might have done to upset her?

sentences.note: **make her mad** 는 "화나게 하다" 를 말할 때 가장 흔하게 쓰는 표현입니다. 조금 부드럽게 말하려면 **upset her** 로 바꿉니다 — 화보다는 속상하게 했다는 쪽입니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 10 | Friends

sentences.ko: 잠깐 나랑 이쪽으로 좀 와 볼래?
sentences.text: Will you come here with me for a minute?

alts.text: Got a sec? Come with me.
Would you mind stepping over here with me for a moment?

sentences.note: **for a minute** 는 진짜 1분이 아니라 "잠깐만" 이라는 뜻입니다. 사람을 따로 불러내 조용히 얘기할 때 쓰고, 더 편한 자리에서는 **Got a sec** 이라고 물어봅니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 10 | Friends

sentences.ko: 걔가 내 옷차림 가지고 좀 놀리더라.
sentences.text: She kind of teased me about how I dress.

alts.text: Got teased about my clothes a bit.
I was teased by her about the way I dress.

sentences.note: **teased me about** 은 악의 없이 장난스럽게 놀리는 것이라 험담과는 다릅니다. 앞에 붙은 **kind of** 는 "좀, 살짝" 하고 수위를 낮추는 말이에요.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 10 | Friends
